articles.title: More Room for Difference, Less Room for Change: Generative AI and Psychosocial Disabilities at Work
articles.abstract: The growing incorporation of generative AI into work life creates new possibilities for accommodating diverse ways of functioning while raising questions about the reproduction of existing organisational norms. Drawing on qualitative research on how people with psychosocial disabilities use generative AI at work, this article examines the reconfiguration of relations between workers, working processes, and expected outcomes in work assemblages, which are mediated through generative AI. First, generative AI serves as workplace accommodation, helping participants adapt work to their ways of functioning. Second, it mediates between diverse work processes and expected outcomes, allowing workers to work in their own ways while producing outputs that meet workplace standards. Third, generative AI helps create digital doubles that communicate and present themselves in normative ways. By mediating between diverse ways of working and standardised organisational expectations, generative AI can reinforce existing organisational norms rather than encourage the systemic changes needed for workplace inclusion.

articles.title: Doing Less and Giving More: How Parents Compensate and Reinforce Through Different Forms of Investment.
articles.abstract: Research on parental investments often assumes that parents either compensate for or reinforce differences between children. I argue that parents do both through different forms of investment, and that which forms they adjust depends on which resource is scarce. When a child’s situation allows it, high-SES parents economize on their time and low-SES parents on their money. Using school-entry rules in 28 educational systems and three waves of TIMSS (2011–2019), I examine how children’s relative age shapes parental investments and household organization. Parents of relatively older children help less with homework and use less tutoring to keep up, but have more books at home and, in some systems, use more tutoring to excel. These patterns are strikingly similar across systems. SES shapes the form of investments parents make. The effect for homework help and books is larger among high-SES families, whereas the effect on tutoring to keep up is larger among low-SES families. Relative age also shapes the household, mothers of relatively older children are more likely to work full-time, regardless of SES. Compensation and reinforcement are thus not rival accounts of parental behavior but responses that run through different forms of investment, shaped by the resources families can spare.

articles.title: From Raw LLMs to Calibrated Silicon Samples: An Empirical Validation and Methodological Debiasing Against the Israeli Voice Index
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Public opinion research faces an acute structural crisis characterized by plummeting response rates, escalating fieldwork costs, and nonresponse bias across polarized demographic strata. Within computational social science, "silicon sampling" (conditioning large language models on socio-demographic personas to simulate survey respondents) has emerged as a promising paradigm. However, existing validation benchmarks frequently rely on aggregate correlations (r = 0.65 to 0.78) that mask substantial intra-question distributional error, while exhibiting severe roleplay decisiveness, mode collapse in international relations, and ideological over-uniformity. This study presents a two-wave empirical validation and methodological debiasing of SekerAI, benchmarked against the September 2026 Israeli Voice Index (N = 751) by the Israel Democracy Institute (IDI). Methodology: We conducted a controlled two-wave experiment across 24 national questions (108 discrete response categories). In Wave 1 (Uncalibrated Baseline, N = 751), synthetic agents generated via census-stratified probability vectors answered standard questionnaire items. In Wave 2 (Calibrated Simulation, N = 751), we engineered four structural debiasing mechanisms: (1) an Epistemic Humility Gate conditioning option selection on news salience and cognitive hesitation; (2) a Subjective Citizen Lens replacing textbook foreign policy with grassroots security skepticism; (3) Relevance-Gated Political-Ideological Anchoring paired with an Economic Pressure Index (1-10) and behavioral decision vectors; and (4) Anti-Hedging Scale Dispersion to prevent artificial mode collapse. Evaluations measured intra-question Total Variation Distance (TVD), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Pearson correlation (r) against a Uniform Null Baseline. Empirical Findings: Wave 1 exhibited strong aggregate correlation (option-level r = 0.804, bloc-level r = 0.862) but suffered from classical LLM distortions: mean TVD of 30.7%, MAE of 13.3 percentage points (pp), and severe "Don't know" under-representation (0.7% vs. 9.3% human mean). Wave 2 improved accuracy across 21 of 24 questions (87.5%): mean TVD dropped by 5.8 pp to 24.9% (a 19% relative error reduction), MAE shrank to 10.9 pp, option-level correlation rose to r = 0.844 (bloc-level r = 0.879), and "Don't know" selection reached 8.7% (within 0.6 pp of humans). Notably, TVD fell by 10.9 pp on international relations (48.2% to 37.3%) and was nearly halved on October 7 intelligence disclosures (20.5% to 10.9%). Conclusion: Raw LLMs cannot serve as faithful synthetic polls out of the box due to systematic decisiveness distortions. However, when grounded in formal survey methodology, calibrated silicon sampling achieves marked distributional convergence toward human benchmarks, offering a transparent instrument for pre-fieldwork diagnostics within the Total Survey Error (TSE) framework.

articles.title: Outskilling, Scepticism, and New Class Boundaries: How Senior Tech Workers Make Sense of GenAI
articles.abstract: This article examines how senior tech workers in the UK perceive and evaluate GenAI, a technology that is shaped by their professional expertise and also increasingly embedded in their everyday work. Based on 30 interviews, including 21 with unionised workers, we approach our sample as a critical case for illuminating latent tensions and conflicts in the tech industry. Our findings reveal that our interviewees are less concerned with deskilling and more with outskilling, understood as the constraining of workers’ opportunities to exercise and develop their expertise. A second theme is the perceived erosion of the learning pipeline between senior and junior workers. Our interviewees criticise juniors for over-relying on GenAI, revealing new boundary-makings within the tech workforce. Finally, we consider the extent to which the social codes of our interviewees point to broader processes of class formation. Across the three themes, a widespread scepticism towards the promises surrounding GenAI emerges.

articles.title: Brazilian Digital Feminism at Two Critical Turning Points: New Elements and Challenges on the Scene (2010–2025)
articles.authors: Isabela Andrade, Nicole Brito de Sena
articles.abstract: In the 2010s, a new feminist consciousness gained strength in Brazil (Facchini et al., 2020). Driven by the internet, a new feminist “way of being” and “way of doing” emerged, characterized by digital activism led by young women and marked by intergenerational conflicts (Sarmento, 2021). These tensions challenge the centrality of digital tools in relation to in-person and collective feminist practices. In this sense, there is a critique that feminism is not merely about posting long texts or viral videos on social media. However, withdrawing from online spaces is no longer an option, once conservative forces that have being reacted to feminist and LGBTQ+ advances (Biroli, Vaggione & Machado, 2020), also use social media to spread their agendas. In light of this scenario, we ask: how have digital feminist strategies been shaped in response to recent political changes? The discussions presented here stem from an ongoing exploratory study based on data collected from online interviews conducted with 40 feminist activists with diverse profiles between 2023 and 2025. The selection of participants followed a non-probabilistic sampling method (Merriam, 2009), mainly using the snowball technique to capture different forms of engagement in feminist activism and the meanings attributed to online participation in the current context. The interviews followed a semi-structured guide, lasted on average one hour, and were fully transcribed. Our hypothesis proposes two main turning points: the first, from 2010 to 2018, corresponds to the “feminist spring” and the early exploration of social media; the second, beginning with Bolsonaro’s election, marks a phase of feminist retreat, characterized by the strengthening of antifeminism and by new algorithmic logics that demand strategic repositioning. Through their narratives, the interviewees also allow us to reflect on the process of affective polarization online, which exposes feminists to yet another face of gender-based violence (Setenta, 2024).

articles.title: Polyphemus in the Cave and the Absence of Public Persuasion: An Institutional Analysis of Status-Demographic Codes from Early Joseon to Colonial and Post-Colonial Surveillance Enclosures
articles.abstract: This study investigates a foundational void in the constitutional and legal history of the Korean peninsula: the structural non-existence of political persuasion. In comparative state formation, deliberative persuasion functioned not as moral benevolence, but as a formal transaction cost extorted by the material capacity of direct producers to execute systemic rupture—exemplified by Roman republican plebeian secessions. Across five centuries of the Joseon dynasty and its twentieth-century transformations, peninsular state power operated upon an inverse trajectory. The governed were never constituted as horizontal negotiating subjects possessing juridical standing; rather, they were regimentally quarantined within patriarchal units of production under centralized bureaucratic oversight. By examining the institutional continuity of status codes, colonial cadastral dispossession, the reception of Bismarckian-Meiji Pandectist jurisprudence in the 1958 Civil Code, and the permanent reproduction of extraordinary penal regimes, this monograph demonstrates that the post-colonial republic preserved and refined the coercive machinery of the inherited state apparatus. Rather than fulfilling an emancipated compact among co-legislating citizens, this historical development culminated in an unbroken bureaucratized enclosure. Perfected through the 1968 universal biometric registration system and managed by a credentialed technocratic caste, the contemporary state definitively fixed the direct producer where peninsular statecraft has always confined him: an administered asset, governed entirely without the procedural friction of persuasion.

articles.title: The Pricing-by-Design Matrix: Classifying Resort Activities by Experience Design and Pricing Status
articles.abstract: Maldivian resorts operate in an island setting characterised by lagoons, reefs and a tropical climate. Differentiation can arise from how each resort combines accommodation, facilities, service delivery and the experiences offered to guests. This paper proposes the Pricing-by-Design Matrix, an activity-level instrument for examining experience design and pricing within that service-product mix. The design dimension assesses evidence of five principles: theme, positive cues, removal of negative cues, memorabilia and sensory engagement. The pricing dimension records whether an activity carries an additional charge or is included in a specified reference plan. Crossing the design score with pricing status produces a two-by-two matrix that classifies each activity as a background activity, priced service, designed but given away, or experience offering. A coding protocol specifies how to record the evidence and calculate the Experience Design Completeness Index (EDCI). The pilot examines 17 activities identified in published descriptions and plan terms from two Maldivian resorts. It assessed theme, memorabilia and sensory engagement through a provisional three-principle text index. Positive cues and the removal of negative cues could not be assessed from the published material. Thirteen activities were provisionally classified as priced services and four as background activities. No activity met the text-index design threshold. At the all-inclusive resort, separate pricing was inferred for seven activities absent from the published inclusion list. The paper develops four propositions for further research. Further testing should assess coding reliability, threshold sensitivity and relationships with guest outcomes.

articles.title: Physician-Led Research Infrastructure in a Private Equity–Backed Musculoskeletal Network: An Organizational Case Study
articles.authors: Tesheia Howard-Harris, Gary W. Stewart, Kenneth Ellinger, Melissa Murphy

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Background: Clinical research programs are often described from the perspective of academic departments with established infrastructure. In contrast, large private musculoskeletal practice networks face a different challenge: how to build a durable research structure while maintaining high-volume clinical operations, distributed leadership, and day-to-day practice efficiency. Objective: To describe an early-stage model for building a clinical research structure within a busy physician-led musculoskeletal practice network and to identify the operational, governance, and partnership strategies used to make research feasible in routine practice, including how physician decision-making authority over research was structured within a private equity–backed management services organization. Methods: This descriptive organizational case study drew on a 2024–2025 clinical research infrastructure assessment, including document review, semi-structured interviews with 12 UMP leaders, and two site visits, together with a structured, iterative review of internal strategic planning materials, leadership presentations, quality and patient-reported outcome (PRO) dashboards, and organizational documents from United Musculoskeletal Partners (UMP), interpreted against prior literature on orthopaedic research team development. Interpretations were checked through author consensus and face-validity review by market-level leaders. Results: UMP’s emerging model rests on five practical design choices: 1) starting with a focused research vision tied to patient outcomes and quality benchmarks; 2) placing physician leadership at the center of governance; 3) using external partners strategically to supplement internal capacity; 4) integrating research activities with existing clinical and operational workflows rather than creating a parallel academic structure; and 5) sequencing the work into short-term proof-of-concept projects and longer-term infrastructure building. Participation grew from a three-person founding team to 21 surgeons serving on a cross-site research council without additional compensation. Existing PRO infrastructure had captured 2,721,144 PRO scores by June 2026, with 2025 baseline compliance of 77.23% across participating practices. Conclusion: For high-volume musculoskeletal groups, durable research infrastructure may be most feasible when built as an extension of clinical operations rather than as a separate academic enterprise. A pragmatic, partnership-enabled, physician-led model may allow busy practice networks to generate publishable data, strengthen quality measurement, and create a sustainable pathway toward broader participation in innovation and clinical trials. Within a private equity–backed platform, documented governance preserved physician authority over research priorities, offering a counterexample to the assumption that such ownership necessarily limits physician direction of research.

articles.title: Keep on Keeping On, With a Machine: Artificial Intelligence and the Calibration of Entrepreneurial Persistence
articles.authors: Jiaju Justin Yan, Xiaqing Nancy He, Alan Boss
articles.abstract: Entrepreneurs increasingly turn to artificial intelligence (AI) when deciding whether to continue a struggling venture, yet persistence theory locates the antecedents of persistence either within the entrepreneur or within human social networks. We theorize AI as a distinct, non-human antecedent of entrepreneurial persistence. Building on the psychological resource approach to persistence, escalation and threshold theories, and the AI Entrepreneurial Agency Framework, we distinguish two pathways. Through a resource pathway, AI supplies psychological resources that raise persistence intensity and loosen its dependence on the entrepreneur's internal resources. Through an epistemic pathway, AI shapes the feedback on which persistence decisions rest and thereby governs persistence calibration, which we define as the responsiveness of persistence to diagnostic disconfirming evidence. Five propositions specify when the pathways combine into AI-amplified escalation, how the Knightian uncertainty of the decision widens a gap between confidence and calibration, and how agentic AI attenuates the decision points at which founders confront adversity. A temporal extension explains how sustained AI scaffolding can render persistence fragile. The framework reconciles optimistic and pessimistic accounts of AI in entrepreneurship and offers testable implications for small business owners, advisors, and AI designers.

articles.title: Who sees the sea? Sea-view potential by façade and floor from cadastral LoD1 models on the Costa del Sol
articles.abstract: Views are among the most valued and least measured attributes of a home. We present an open-data method that estimates the sea-view potential of every free façade of every residential building at three floors (ground, middle and top; other floors take the nearest of them), from cadastral footprints with floor counts and a national terrain model. Run for 158,060 buildings of 21 municipalities on Spain's Costa del Sol in under an hour on two cores, it finds that 52 % of buildings see some sea from their top floor and 36 % have an open view (20° or more). Traced over a LiDAR surface in a pilot, scores agree with the model's inside cadastral footprints (96.7 % of viewpoints in the same class at 20°), but structures the cadastre does not record lower the sea seen from the top floor by 6.1–9.0° on average. Against the photographs of 93 homes for sale, labelled blind by AI models of two developers with ties decided by the author, the score has an AUC of 0.80 (95 % CI 0.70–0.89; 0.81 against the first-round labels); at 20° it is sensitive (0.90) but not specific (0.45). Dwelling figures depend on how dwellings are allocated to façades and floors: 42 % of dwellings are on a floor with open-view potential under the main rule, and 12–45 % across the allocation, geometry and vegetation scenarios tested. As an application, higher-income census sections tend to have more modelled view potential within municipalities, with uncertain size and fragile inference (about two effective clusters); on terrain alone the difference largely disappears. Code and façade-level data reproduce the main results.

articles.title: Credibility and Connection: A Field Experiment Comparing the Democratic Effects of Traditional News, News Influencers, and Social-First News
articles.authors: Erin Wertz, Wonjeong Jo, Emma Hoes, Magdalena Wojcieszak
articles.abstract: The news media ecosystem is undergoing substantial changes; news avoidance is growing, news influencers are becoming prominent, and mainstream news outlets increasingly draw from influencers to design “social-first” content for social media platforms. Yet, the effects of these new news producers are not well understood, particularly compared to those of traditional news. We develop a framework distinguishing traditional news, news influencers, and social-first news through three pathways (informational, relational, experiential), positing that distinctive content features influence audience perceptions (credibility, social presence and engagement), which — in turn — influence democratic attitudes. We test this framework in a preregistered, two-week longitudinal online field experiment (N = 1,284), randomly assigning U.S. Instagram and TikTok users to follow traditional news, news influencers, social first news, or non-news control accounts. Following all news types increases trust in social media news, while traditional news additionally increases trust in news more broadly, and those assigned to follow traditional news report the highest intent to continue following these accounts post-study. Mediation analyses support the informational and relational pathways, but not the experiential: credibility predicts greater knowledge, discernment, and trust, while social presence predicts greater political interest and trust. These patterns do not depend on compliance, prior news consumption, or socio-demographics. By classifying all videos posted by our treatment news accounts during the study period, we also show that theoretically salient content features differ consistently across types of news. We discuss the implications of our findings for the theorizing of the online information ecosystem, and for journalistic practitioners.

articles.title: The Justice Engagement Gap: Comparative Institutions and Anti-Trafficking Enforcement in the United States, Brazil, and China
articles.abstract: Human trafficking is nearly universal in law but highly uneven in prosecution. Existing cross-national research usually examines either trafficking prevalence or anti-trafficking enforcement, leaving unclear whether states respond at levels proportionate to estimated need. This article introduces the Justice Engagement Gap (JEG) framework to compare estimated trafficking prevalence with observable prosecutorial engagement while avoiding false numerical precision. The framework classifies trafficking prevalence levels and prosecutorial engagement separately, then evaluates whether their relationship indicates a narrow, moderate, high, or severe justice gap. I apply the framework to three institutionally contrasting cases: the United States, Brazil, and China. The comparison identifies three distinct pathways linking formal criminalization to uneven enforcement. In the United States, a narrow gap coexists with strong prosecutorial capacity but persistent underenforcement of labor trafficking. In Brazil, a high gap reflects fragmented federal coordination, dual legal tracks for trafficking and “slave labor,” and judicial bottlenecks that prevent investigations from yielding timely convictions. In China, a high gap reflects a qualitatively different problem: state perpetration, data suppression, and the absence of independent accountability. The article argues that anti-trafficking outcomes are best under- stood as institutional products shaped by capacity, coordination, transparency, and regime incentives rather than by statutory criminalization alone.

articles.title: How normative claims guide engineers under value pluralism: The “Portasello” model of collaborative viability and value interfaces
articles.abstract: How can normative claims guide engineers under conditions of value pluralism? Existing approaches in the engineering and engineering management literatures, including value engineering, value management, and value-sensitive design, explain how values inform decision-making but leave underdeveloped how practitioners act when multiple legitimate values remain in tension. This paper develops a contextual account of action guidance drawing on Raz's theory of exclusionary reasons, Tomasello's account of socially stratified intentionality, and a conception of engineering as participation in collaborative value chains derived from Porter. It argues that engineers confront value pluralism not by resolving conflicts through value ranking or optimization, but committing to a higher-order norm of collaborative viability, which functions as a constitutive condition of engineering collaboration rather than as a competing substantive value. Building on this insight, the paper introduces the “Portasello” model, a framework of how engineers organize, communicate, and reconcile values through the management of intra-agent and inter-agent value interfaces. The model shows how values acquire action guiding force within collaborative practice by being translated into workable courses of action through coordination across the value chain. Rather than treating engineering as the application or pursuit of pre-given values, the paper reconceptualizes engineering as a practice of interface management through which diverse values become actionable. The framework further develops a typology of normative failure modes and argues that knowledge of how to sustain collaboration under conditions of persistent value pluralism constitutes a core dimension of engineering expertise.

articles.title: Civic Architecture: A Statement of the Research Program
articles.abstract: Civic architecture is a design science of democratic life. It holds that democratic capacity is produced by institutions that convert participation into binding civic consequence through durable pathways, and that where those pathways are absent, participation erodes the capacity it is meant to build. This statement sets out the research program as it stands in November 2026: its account of hollowness and managerial professionalism; the two dimensions of one civic ontology; standing, office, and structural cognition; four design elements and the rules that combine them; repair, trust, and the outside order; a consent standard; the method and the evidence standard, applied first to the program's own case; and the questions that remain open. It replaces nothing in the 2025 deposits, names what has changed since them, and states what the program claims and what it does not.

articles.title: Towards a praxeology of lay and artistic improvisation
articles.abstract: This article calls for a closer connection between praxeology and improvisation. Praxeology is a social scientific approach to action that was developed by ethnomethodology and conversation analysis. Deeply inspired by phenomenology and its insistence on belonging to the world, praxeology approaches action as a concrete engagement with reality. Confronted with indeterminacy stemming from situatedness (indexicality) and contingency, we figure out how to discover and invent order and meaning by engaging with our socio-material environment. This process of endogenous determination is of special relevance to improvisation both in artistic and everyday (“lay”) settings. A praxeological approach to improvisation can be useful to specify what it is, rather than unfavorably comparing it to other forms of action, and to study improvisation rigorously through the systematic use of video-recorded natural data that preserve as much as possible of the situated process of endogenous determination. While there are convergences between praxeology and improvisation (scholars and practitioners), this article invites to increase their mutual understanding and to produce more praxeological studies on lay and artistic improvisation practices.

articles.title: Where Americans Moved — and the Money That Moved With Them: Interstate Migration of Households and Income in IRS Statistics of Income Data, 2022–2023
articles.abstract: Using IRS Statistics of Income migration data for 2022–2023, this paper maps interstate migration of U.S. households and the adjusted gross income (AGI) that moved with them. Among 3,966,932 interstate mover households, Texas recorded the largest net household gain (+56,473) and California the largest loss (−100,397), while Florida captured the largest net AGI inflow (+$20.65 billion). Results are reported on an interstate basis with Census population denominators for per-capita comparisons, and the 2022–2023 series break is documented.

articles.title: Two Varvaras: Was Semennikova the Oldest Documented Woman in Russian History?
articles.abstract: Varvara Konstantinovna Semennikova (née Dyakonova; registered as Androsova at her 1944 marriage), a resident of the Anabar ulus of Yakutia, died on 9 March 2008. The birth year 1890 attributed to her in the 2000s would make her 117 years old at death. The attribution rests on an 1890 parish-register entry for a daughter of Konstantin Stefanovich Dyakonov of the 2nd Khatyga nasleg. This paper examines, for the first time, an alternative entry recording the birth on 28 September 1907 (O.S.) of Varvara, daughter of Konstantin Nikolaevich Dyakonov and Feodosia Petrovna of the 3rd Khatyga nasleg. Her earlier passport age, family recollections, the 1944 marriage certificate and a 1926–1927 household census card found by the author are compared. Of particular weight is a 2005 newspaper report that Varvara herself believed her second husband (born 1917) to be 11, not 27, years younger than she was. Had she been born in 1890, she would have been 53 at the 1944 wedding, while by her own reckoning she was about 37 and her husband about 27; an error of this size in adulthood is unlikely. As shown by Zak and Gibbs [15], deeming a claimed age unvalidated does not require proving the alternative hypothesis: it suffices to establish a plausible alternative scenario whose probability, given the available evidence, is incompatible with the degree of certainty required for validation. In the present case the evidence as a whole agrees substantially better with Varvara Semennikova's birth in 1907 than in 1890. At the same time, the identification of the claimant with the specific 1907 register entry remains unproven.

articles.title: The wealth of algorithms: generative AI, jobs and inequality in a global dynamic CGE model
articles.abstract: This paper models how generative artificial intelligence (AI) affects jobs, wages and inequality across the world economy. Few doubt that it will change the economy; what nobody yet knows is how. Workers, firms and governments want to know whose jobs and pay will change, who will capture the gains and which countries will come out ahead, well before the evidence can tell them. This paper does not try to forecast that future. Its contribution is a quantitative framework for understanding what drives AI’s economic effects, what they depend on, and what follows for policy. We add AI to a global dynamic computable general equilibrium (CGE) model that tracks production, trade, investment and employment year by year to 2040 in 23 regions. AI does some tasks inside each occupation and makes workers more productive in others. When AI does a task, we start from a 27% saving on its labour cost, the average Acemoglu (2025) draws from two workplace experiments. We run a central scenario and 68 alternatives that vary how fast and how widely AI is adopted, what it costs, how far it replaces rather than helps workers and how labour markets adjust. How cheap and capable AI becomes, and how widely firms adopt it, decide the size of the gain: by 2040 world GDP ends about 1% to 15% above a path without AI in our main scenarios (about 7% in the central case). It reaches about 35% in an extreme case where AI becomes 30% a year more efficient (15 to 25% if AI keeps improving but more slowly over time). Most of the gain goes to owners of capital in almost every scenario. Who shares in it depends on who owns capital and on the extent to which AI replaces rather than helps workers. In the central case capital’s share of world income rises by about 4 points, clerks’ real pay ends roughly 13 to 22% below the no-AI path in the large economies, and within rich economies the Gini coefficient of household income rises by about 2 to 3.5 points. If job losses last, the world gain against the no-AI baseline in 2040 is 5.4% against 6.8%, and labour income falls further everywhere. Based on these results, we then test several illustrative AI policies to see how they change the outcomes and their distributional effects. Each does a different job: support for changing jobs mainly protects workers’ pay, keeping AI cheap mainly protects output, and only sharing AI’s capital income narrows inequality noticeably. The policies are illustrative and largely unfunded in the model, so their gains are likely inflated.

articles.title: Algorithmic Gatekeepers: Artificial Intelligence, Financial Intermediation, and the Disruption of China’s IPO Market
articles.abstract: Initial public offerings in China pass through a dense chain of gatekeepers: sponsors, auditors, exchange reviewers, the securities regulator, and a retail-dominated investor base. Artificial intelligence now enters every link in that chain at once. It writes disclosures, verifies them, screens them for regulators, informs the investors who price them, and increasingly forms the core of the issuers that seek listing. This paper develops a theory of how AI disrupts an IPO market that operates as a state-orchestrated certification system. Drawing on signaling theory, the economics of certification, institutional theory, and the view of AI as an entrepreneurial actor, we argue that AI lowers the cost of producing information while leaving the cost of producing credible information intact. Seven propositions trace where the residual cost of credibility moves: toward an inverted U-shaped link between AI-generated disclosure and informativeness, a shift in intermediary rents from reputation to verification, an advantage for algorithmically legible issuers, an earlier inflection point in the effect of positive sentiment on IPO performance, attribution-dependent penalties for AI issuers, scope-contingent gains for intermediaries, and state pacing as a boundary condition. The theory explains why AI can raise market throughput and lower signal informativeness at the same time.

articles.title: Contract Form and the Persistence of Executive Discretion Over Foreign Capital in Bangladesh
articles.abstract: Foreign investors earn returns from public contracts under every kind of government, so their presence cannot explain how much a state gives up. This article asks what does. It follows six episodes in Bangladesh's electricity sector from the late 1990s to 2026, coding each by its route into the state, the type of foreign benefit, the form of the payment commitment and the contract's later history. The argument is that concentrated authority lets a government commit public revenue quickly, and that the form of the resulting contract then sets how costly correction becomes. Vernon's obsolescing bargain predicts that leverage drifts toward the host state once capital is sunk. Take-or-pay agreements, dedicated plants and sovereign-backed credit can block that drift, so the bargain never becomes obsolete. The persistence claim is the best supported of four propositions tested. The 2024 repeal of the special procurement law left existing contracts valid, and the Godda terms were still disputed in 2026. At least 11 percent of import capacity, and at most about 28 percent, came through open competition, while a single dedicated plant accounts for 56 percent. Comparison cases from Bangladesh's rental plants, Indonesia and Pakistan show that exit came at contract expiry or at a price in compensation, haircuts or longer terms. The record supports neither a finding of policy capture nor one of illegal enrichment. It supports a narrower claim about institutional form, and about who can ask a state to think again.

articles.title: Persistent Rating Disagreement, Measurement Robustness, and Information Reliability in Sustainable Finance: Implications for ESG Transparency and Evidence-Based Sustainability Governance in Chinese Listed Companies
articles.abstract: This study investigates cross-provider environmental, social, and governance (ESG) rating disagreement, temporal persistence, and measurement robustness, with particular emphasis on improving the reliability of sustainability information for ESG management and financial decision-making. Using an unbalanced panel of 1,323 firm-year observations representing 377 Chinese listed companies during 2019–2024, the study compares MSCI- and FTSE Russell-attributed assessments. Disagreement is operationalised through percentile-rank, standardised-score, and min-max transformations. The analysis integrates descriptive statistics, consecutive-year Spearman correlation, exploratory panel regressions, firm-clustered inference, multiple-testing adjustments, and reproducible computational verification. The mean absolute percentile-rank disagreement is 0.2493, indicating appreciable differences in relative corporate assessments. A consecutive-year Spearman correlation of approximately 0.493 demonstrates moderate temporal persistence. Alternative harmonisation procedures produce different inferential conclusions concerning exploratory financial associations, particularly firm size, highlighting the importance of measurement-sensitive interpretation. The study integrates disagreement magnitude, temporal persistence, and measurement robustness within a reproducible framework, extending ESG divergence research beyond isolated provider comparisons. Drawing on Institutional Theory and information asymmetry, it positions ESG disagreement as an information-governance challenge rather than direct evidence of inaccurate sustainability performance. The findings support systematic provider comparison, transparent rating harmonisation, and sensitivity assessment in ESG information management. Such practices offer a basis for improving evidence scrutiny and decision transparency, subject to limitations concerning secondary-data provenance, panel composition, and observational inference.

articles.title: Persistence in Complex Systems: Knowledge as Medium Decoding Instantiated in Material Transformation
articles.abstract: Theories of knowledge remain split between anthropocentric epistemology, which restricts knowing to conscious representation, and syntactic information theory, which detaches information from the maintenance of systems. This article reframes the problem as one of persistence in complex systems: how is acquired organisation retained, materialised, and reactivated across biological, artefactual, institutional, and computational substrates? Knowledge is defined as the decoding of the regularities that the mediums of an inaccessible reality make available, conserved as path-dependent organisation across an interdependent network of multistable physical supports, and expressed as conditional material transformations of the environment. Drawing on nonequilibrium thermodynamics, cybernetics, autopoiesis, Santa Fe complexity theory, and externalist social theory, the article models persistence through a knowledge cycle of learning, memory, and material encapsulation, which couples dissipative acquisition and expression with multistable conservation. Two distinctions make the thesis precise: explicit, implicit, and implicative tiers of encapsulation, whose limit is set by untuned latent dependencies; and continuity of material support, operational activity, and epistemic organisation, which explains how spores, institutions, and computational models persist across suspended activity. Three refutable propositions predict where transfer, resumption, and transition failures occur, and how recovery depends on whether myths can be revised, and define research lines in natural experiments and artificial-life simulations.

articles.title: Towards a Scientific Theory of Vipassana Meditation: Integrating Buddhist Psychology into Contemporary Psychological Science
articles.abstract: Vipassana meditation in the tradition of S. N. Goenka proposes a detailed psychological model of how suffering is generated, maintained, and potentially reduced. Although meditation and mindfulness have received considerable scientific attention, the original effect pathways proposed within this tradition have rarely been translated into contemporary psychological terminology or systematically compared with established psychological mechanisms. This theoretical paper reconstructs the psychological model underlying S. N. Goenka’s Vipassana tradition and examines its potential correspondence with contemporary psychological science. Central propositions include that (1) psychological suffering is amplified through reaction patterns of craving and aversion; (2) repeated reactions to experiences strengthen conditioned dysfunctional patterns of responding (saṅkhāras); (3) equanimous observation is proposed to interrupt these maladaptive reaction patterns, allowing a natural process of permanent dissolution to unfold (purification); (4) bodily sensations provide an interface through which mental reactions can be modified; and (5) reduced ongoing mental activity may allow previously conditioned psychological material to surface and to become accessible. Research on memory accessibility, acceptance, interoception, and learning supports aspects of this account, without establishing that these processes jointly produce the proposed “purification.” We conceptualize purification as reduced maladaptive influence of stored psychological material, with (a) natural dissolution, (b) extinction learning and (c) memory reconsolidation as candidate mechanisms. Seven propositions guide empirical investigation of this pathway, distinguishing temporary relief from lasting psychological change. Testing these propositions could establish whether concentration and equanimous bodily observation provide trainable skills for accessing difficult psychological material and changing habitual responses, thereby supporting well-being and reducing suffering.

articles.title: The Limits of Official Chinese Nationalism in Online Discourse: A Quantitative Text Analysis Using Language Models
articles.abstract: Official Chinese nationalism rests on the concept of the Chinese nation (Zhonghua minzu), understood as both a nation and a single overarching ethnic community. How do Chinese people receive official nationalism, and what are its limits? Analysing ethnicity-related discussions on Zhihu, I define five dimensions of official nationalism and develop a language model-based classifier that sorts posts into accepting, rejecting and unclear stances. Using a diversity index and logistic regression, I examine the distribution of stances and the relationship between toxic language and similarity to official narratives. BERTopic is then used to explore the arguments behind each stance. Discussions of Chinese nationalism remain diverse online. Accepting posts are less likely to contain toxic language, whereas rejecting posts may turn official narratives into targets of hostility. Official nationalism also struggles to construct a shared ancient history and common bonds among ethnic groups, facing challenges from orthodox Marxist and Han-centred interpretations.

articles.title: Human Capital Management: Principles, Functions, and Priorities in the Context of the Structural-Synergistic Paradigm / Менеджмент людського капіталу: принципи, функції та пріоритети у контексті структурно-синергетичної парадигми

subjects.name: Public Affairs, Public Policy and Public Administration

articles.abstract: Peer-reviewed author’s accepted manuscript, accepted for publication on November 4, 2026, in Economics, Management and Administration (scheduled for Q4 2026).The article is devoted to the development of scientific and theoretical foundations and human capital management practice. The study is based on the author’s approach, according to which human capital in its traditional dimension – as an accumulated stock of knowledge, skills, abilities, and professional experience – is defined from the perspective of the educational and competency-based core belonging to a content-wise significantly broader polystructural complex. The latter, being human capital in its full sense, also includes other types of capitals, forming an emergent whole that has an investment nature, is capable of generating income, and contributes to improving the quality of life of employees and society as a whole through a set of economic and social effects. Under such a paradigm shift, along with the educational and competency-based component as a key subsystem, the architecture of the studied economic phenomenon is structurally and functionally complemented by health capital, social capital, and psychological capital, the nature of interaction between which is determined by the regularities of moderated mediation as a condition for the emergence of systemic synergy. The fundamental difference of the proposed theoretical and methodological framework lies in the fact that within the defined systemic framework, the concept of human capital acquires a holistic rather than fragmentary content, which, inter alia, should be reflected in managerial activity. The purpose of the article is to uncover the properties of human capital under its expanded interpretation, as well as to clarify the principles, functions, and priorities of management in the context of the structural-synergetic paradigm. The methodological basis of the study includes systemic, structural-functional, and synergetic approaches. The article analyzes the processes of formation, actualization, and externalization of human capital subsystems and determines their properties, which became the basis for updating scientific and theoretical foundations and formulating practical recommendations for human capital management as an integral part of management processes in the era of the knowledge economy.

articles.title: The Pressure to Appear Fine: Emotional Suppression, School Belonging, and Psychological Well-Being among High School Students
articles.authors: Ha Phuong Khanh, Nguyen Thi Thuy Ngan
articles.abstract: Many adolescents answer “I’m fine” when they are not. This study examined the associations among school belonging, the pressure to appear fine, expressive suppression and psychological well-being in Vietnamese high school students, including whether suppression mediates the link between the pressure and well-being and whether the pressure mediates the link between belonging and suppression. Students in grades 10 to 12 completed an online questionnaire in September and October 2026, and 120 valid responses were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model met the criteria for reliability and validity. Two of the eight hypotheses were supported: the pressure to appear fine was strongly associated with expressive suppression (β = 0.684, p < 0.001), and school belonging with psychological well-being (β = 0.581, p < 0.001). Belonging was not significantly associated with the pressure or with suppression, neither the pressure nor suppression was significantly associated with well-being, and no indirect path was significant. In this sample, the expectation of looking composed is closely tied to how students manage emotional expression, whereas school belonging is the factor most clearly associated with how well they feel.

articles.title: Computing The Incomputable? Artificial Intelligence and Entrepreneurial Decision Making Under Uncertainty
articles.authors: Miles Robin, Leo Will, M Pyad
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence promises to reduce the uncertainty that surrounds entrepreneurial decisions by predicting demand, scanning environments, and evaluating strategic alternatives at negligible cost. We argue that this promise is conditional on the type of uncertainty a decision involves. Drawing on real options reasoning and research distinguishing risk from Knightian uncertainty, we theorize that AI reduces uncertainty that can be resolved through information but cannot resolve uncertainty that is revealed only through action. When decision makers fail to distinguish the two, AI produces uncertainty compression, a condition in which perceived uncertainty falls faster than actual uncertainty, leading entrepreneurs to abandon flexibility and commit prematurely to irreversible investments. We contrast two modes of AI use. In oracle mode, AI is used to resolve uncertainty and select a single course of action. In generator mode, AI is used to expand, stage, and monitor a portfolio of real options. We develop propositions specifying when each mode improves decisions and how entrepreneurial theorizing and competitive diffusion of AI condition these effects. The framework reframes AI not as a substitute for entrepreneurial judgment under uncertainty but as a technology that changes the economics of flexibility.

articles.title: Model Praktik Eco Social Work dalam Perlindungan dan Pengelolaan Lingkungan Hidup di Indonesia: Sintesis Konseptual
articles.abstract: Environmental issues have social dimensions that affect livelihoods, health, community relations, access to resources, and the social functioning of individuals and groups. Environmental protection and management therefore require more than technical and administrative instruments; they also require approaches that assess social impacts, strengthen participation, protect vulnerable groups, and build community capacity. This article develops a conceptual practice model of Eco Social Work to explain the contribution of social work to environmental protection and management in Indonesia. It uses a conceptual synthesis of literature on ecological social work, community development, participation, collaborative governance, and the practice domains addressed in the developing Eco Social Work book. The synthesis proposes a six-stage model: socio-ecological context, socio-ecological assessment, intervention planning, implementation and collaboration, monitoring-evaluation-learning, and socio-ecological outcomes and sustainability. The model positions social workers as professionals who integrate social dimensions into environmental processes through planning, social impact assessment, environmental education, community empowerment, advocacy, mediation, and institutional strengthening. The proposed model remains a conceptual framework and requires empirical examination and refinement. Its contribution is to articulate a practice pathway connecting the mandate of social work with environmental governance while respecting the technical and legal authority of other professions.

articles.title: Constitutional Unilateralism and Federal Fragmentation in Somalia: Contested Constitutional Change, Intergovernmental Consent, and the 2024-2026 Amendments
articles.abstract: Somalia's federal settlement rests on the 2012 Provisional Constitution, which deferred central questions concerning the allocation of powers and resources, the structure of the judiciary, the status of the capital, and the relationship between federal and state constitutions. The constitutional amendments adopted in March 2024 and March 2026 were presented by the federal government as the completion of a review that had run for more than a decade. They were opposed by significant political actors, by the administrations of Puntland and Jubaland, and later by the leadership of South West State. This article asks whether the resulting disputes share a common mechanism, described here as constitutional unilateralism: the alteration of constitutional terms, electoral rules, or intergovernmental arrangements without the participation or agreement reasonably required of the units whose authority or status is affected. The article distinguishes three questions that are frequently merged: whether the required amendment procedure was followed, whether consultation and agreement obligations were satisfied, and what institutional consequences followed. It examines the record for Puntland, Jubaland, South West State, and Hirshabelle; the November 2026 confrontation between the Presidency and the Supreme Court over the judicial treatment of term extensions; and the implications for the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia and the wider security transition. The evidence supports a narrower claim than a single causal story. Contested constitutional change did not create Somalia's political disputes, and in several cases it intersected with conflicts that were already under way. It nevertheless made cooperation harder where it overlapped with unresolved disputes over power, leadership, representation, and security, and it narrowed the space for negotiated settlement. The article concludes that the durability of Somalia's federal order depends less on the formal adoption of a text than on procedures capable of sustaining intergovernmental consent, and on an authenticated constitutional and electoral record that all parties accept as authoritative.

articles.title: When the Melting Pot Becomes a Stressor: Changes in Racial Composition and Psychological Distress among Non-Hispanic Whites
articles.authors: Pui Yin Cheung, David S. Curtis, Ming Wen
articles.abstract: Residential diversity has risen across the United States, yet its implications for the mental health of Whites, the dominant racial group, remain poorly understood. Integrating racial threat theory, the ideologies of whiteness, and the stress process model, we ask (1) whether declining neighborhood White presence and the presence of specific racial/ethnic groups are associated with psychological distress, and (2) whether perceived neighborhood disorder and distrust, physical decay, social integration, and discrimination explain these associations. Analyzing three waves of the Midlife in the United States study (11,772 person-waves) with person fixed effects and inverse-probability-of-censoring weights, we find that declines in White proportion, and increases in Hispanic presence, are associated with greater distress. Disorder and distrust (18.5%) and social integration (13.1%) mediate the White-proportion association; disorder also mediates Black and Hispanic associations, whereas decay and discrimination do not. Demographic change thus becomes race-neutral distress for the dominant group.

articles.title: The Cloud-Pattern Illusion: Falsifiability, Transferability, and the Market for Discretionary Trading Education
articles.abstract: Traders who ask for a method that works do not receive, in the usual sense, a method. They receive a repertoire: a chart-reading practice that is described only by example, a lexicon of pattern names, and a repertoire of reasons why any given application of the pattern did not work. This paper argues that that repertoire is not a theory of markets. A theory must state conditions under which it is wrong and must show that its competence is stable across a residue of cases rather than undefeated only by its own redescription. Discretionary pattern trading fails both requirements. The pattern's content is indexed to the trader's discretion: the same configuration is readable as a valid signal, a transitional form, or a counter-example depending on what happened next, while the method's defence proceeds by attributing failure to the trader's application rather than the method's falsity. The paper shows that a single empirical success cannot absorb the failures implied by that asymmetry because the repertoire's asymmetry is systematic. The contribution is conceptual: to distinguish a pattern's descriptive appeal and the trader's experienced competence from the informational and institutional conclusions that a market for trading education draws from them, and in a companion paper to show how the translation of that competence into a disability claim functions as an institutional mechanism of attribution shifting. AI assistance disclosure: The author used AI tools for translation from Persian and copy-editing. The ideas, analysis, data and conclusions are the author's own. The author reviewed the full text, verified every cited source, and takes full responsibility for the content.

articles.title: The Effect of Interest Rate Changes on Bank Profitability and Credit Growth: The Decoupling of Price and Quantity Instruments in Türkiye (2021-2026)
articles.abstract: This paper examines the effect of the policy rate on bank profitability and credit growth in Türkiye over 2021-2026, placing at its centre the relationship between the price instrument of monetary policy (the policy rate) and its quantity instruments (reserve requirements tied to credit growth). The period constitutes an unusual natural experiment, spanning three distinct policy regimes: deeply negative real-rate easing (2021-mid-2023), rapid high-amplitude tightening (mid-2023-2024), and a prolonged plateau of constant rates following gradual normalisation (2025-2026). Using indicators derived from published aggregate data of the BRSA, the CBRT, TurkStat and the Banks Association of Türkiye, three findings emerge. First, the gap between nominal and real profitability is systematic: sector return on equity has remained below inflation without interruption since 2020, recovering to -2.8% in real terms in 2025 before falling back to an annualised -6.3% in the first seven months of 2026; disinflation has therefore not by itself repaired real profitability. Second, what drives profitability is not the level of the policy rate but the direction and speed of its change: because liabilities reprice faster than assets, easing cycles widen margins through a repricing gain that is exhausted once rates are held constant. The 86 basis point decline in the gross net interest margin and the 230 basis point compression of the TL loan-deposit spread in April 2026 are a direct observation of this mechanism. Third, and as the paper's principal original contribution, where quantity constraints bind, the interest rate channel is second-order for credit growth: the 2% eight-week growth ceiling set for non-SME Turkish lira loans in May 2026 implies an annual nominal ceiling of 13.7%, i.e. a real contraction of roughly 13.5% at current inflation. Realised credit growth, at an annualised 34.2%, nonetheless substantially exceeds these ceilings. The paper conceptualises this gap as a regulatory wedge and attributes it to leakage arising from exemption scope, segment composition and exchange rate effects. The findings indicate that modelling transmission in Türkiye through a single price variable is misleading, and that regulatory quantity constraints must be explicitly internalised. English-language working paper, also available on SSRN: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7638938. Original Turkish version: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22852342. AI disclosure: The author reports using Fable 5.1 during statistical analysis and checking calculations and results using Excel. This English translation was prepared with OpenAI ChatGPT. No new empirical analysis was performed in preparing the translation.

articles.title: Breaking the contract: Imagining the reader in online content on synthetic creative fiction book writing
articles.abstract: Synthetic fiction book writing, wholly or partly created by generative AI, can challenge the implicit contract between readers and writers, reshaping reader identity. This qualitative analysis of online content examines how readers are imagined in response. Readers are framed as indiscriminate consumers or insightful detectors, within a destabilised reader–writer contract.

articles.title: Early Screen Time, Children's Mental Well-Being and Physical Health: Intersectional Inequalities by Socioeconomic Status, Gender and Ethnicity
articles.abstract: In recent years, inequalities in child well-being and health have persisted strongly, while digital technologies have become increasingly embedded in early childhood. However, how early screen exposure relates to these inequalities remains unclear. To address this gap, this study develops an intersectional framework to examine how early-childhood screen time shapes subsequent mental well-being and physical health outcomes. We analyze high-quality longitudinal time-diary data from the Longitudinal Study of Australian Children (LSAC), following children across four waves from ages 0 to 7. Lagged two-way fixed-effects models estimate the association between prior screen time and subsequent psychosocial health (a validated measure of child mental well-being) and Body Mass Index (BMI; a marker of physical health). On average, screen time is not associated with psychosocial health, and only weekend screen time is associated with very small increases in BMI. Yet, this relationship differs substantially across population groups. Screen time predicts poorer psychosocial health among low-SES boys, but not among high-SES boys. Also, early screen time predicts higher BMI among girls, low-SES children, and children from national-majority backgrounds, particularly low-SES national-majority children. These findings indicate that the consequences of early screen exposure are socially stratified at the intersection of SES, gender, and ethnicity, with different patterns for mental well-being and physical health. Overall, this study offers a novel intersectional framework for understanding early screen time as a driver of social inequalities in child mental well-being and physical health.

articles.title: A Job That Comes with an Audience: Night Work and the Wage of Being Seen
articles.abstract: Adam Smith counted public admiration as part of the reward of distinguished talent. He treated money as the price of the discredit that some talents carry. This article argues that Japanese night work has routinized that admiration. Hostess and host clubs turn recognition into an everyday return, recorded or displayed, that ordinary workers earn when named customers choose them again and again. Each club gives newcomers a small charisma of office, which they can turn into a following of their own. I call this return the audience wage and separate it from approval, visibility and customer loyalty. The argument draws on Weber's routinization of charisma and on Etzrodt's pairing of alienation ("lifeless form") and anomie ("formless life"). Entry-level day work offers form without being seen. Unpaid self-promotion offers being seen without form. Night work bundles the two, and the bundle produces a new alienation: workers become bound to a persona and an audience they made. The article proposes that the social change lies at the entrance to adult work. It derives seven propositions, including a compensating-differential test and a test based on Japan's 2025 advertising restrictions. Three of its predictions are made by no rival account.

articles.title: Representation of Indigenous Identities in Coke Studio Pakistan: An Analysis of Cultural Narrative and Digital Platform Dynamics
articles.abstract: This study explores how indigenous identities are portrayed in Coke Studio Pakistan, a major musical platform in the country and analyzes the influence of digital media on their cultural identities. Three purposively selected songs (2022-2025) are analyzed via NVivo, through Stuart Hall’s (1997) of cultural representation and Henry Jenkins (2006) participatory framework. The thematic qualitative analysis revealed a dialectical tension where audience feel pride when regional artists are given platform to showcase their talent and culture. But its growing focus towards global shift and collaboration is starting to blur the cultural authenticity which the platform aims to offer. This research expands the understanding of cultural representation, media control and morality of showcasing the marginalized voices on a wider platform

articles.title: The Entertainment Value System: A Framework for Value Creation and Value Capture in Entertainment
articles.abstract: In contemporary entertainment, content produced by studios, broadcasters, creators, brands and audiences competes for the same scarce resource: attention. Platform mediation, which places all of this content side by side in the same feeds, has made this convergence evident. It blurs the traditional boundaries between the "entertainment industry", "advertising" and "user-generated content", and brings back to the centre a long-standing question in the economics of creative goods: who captures the value that so many actors help to create? This paper proposes the Entertainment Value System (EVS), defined as the system of positions and processes through which the value generated by entertainment – cultural, relational and economic – is created by many actors and captured by few, depending on control over rights, the audience relationship, data and risk. The EVS combines two components. The first is a position map that crosses intellectual property ownership with control of the audience relationship, identifying four positions (owner, integrated system, supplier, access gatekeeper) and a cross-cutting risk dimension. The second is a process map structured in four levels – cultural context, actors and resources, value creation mechanisms, value capture and outcomes – crossed by an axis of risk, investment and governance. Five propositions are derived from the model: cultural embeddedness, ecosystem interdependence, audience participation, platform mediation and asymmetric value capture. The framework is illustrated through five cases and translated into a research agenda with possible constructs and measurement indicators.

articles.title: The Boxology Method and Box World Game: A Dialogic Visual Inquiry Method for Visual Literacy, Participatory Research, and Science Communication
articles.abstract: In an increasingly image-rich and mediatized society, the ability to critically engage with, interpret, and communicate through images has become an essential competence for students and researchers across disciplines. This chapter introduces the visual research game Box World and the Boxology visual inquiry method that it operationalizes. Box World was conceived by the author through empirical research in science communication and developed in creative collaboration with the artist Vinik. Building on the game and its subsequent applications, the Boxology method was conceptualized and developed by the author. Both are grounded in the principles of visual inquiry and participatory research. Depending on the context, the method and its game function as a pedagogical approach for cultivating visual literacy and critical reflection, an arts-based research method for generating qualitative data, and a participatory science communication practice for engaging publics with research in accessible, creative, and interactive ways. Through dialogic engagement with open-ended visuals, participants co-construct meaning, negotiate interpretations, surface implicit assumptions, and reflect on complex issues related to science, technology, and society. The chapter demonstrates how dialogic visual inquiry can simultaneously strengthen visual literacy, support participatory research, generate qualitative research insights, and enrich science dissemination practices.

articles.title: Color Meme Theory: A Socio-Ecological Genetic Framework of Color Affordance, Psychological Association, Cultural Coding, and Memetic Misrecognition
articles.abstract: This paper proposes Color Meme Theory, a framework for analyzing how memes circulate as socially perceived units that acquire color-like meanings, affective values, and evaluative force. By connecting meme theory, color psychology, warning coloration, internet meme studies, and organizational communication, it addresses how the perceived “color” of a meme shapes its reception and social consequences. Color-meme formation is examined through four layers: biological affordances, psychological and emotional associations, material properties, and cultural coding. The framework distinguishes Black, White, Red, Yellow, Green, Gray, Blue, and Pink Memes. Black Memes mediate contamination and labeling; White Memes depend on purity and fragile legitimacy; Red Memes carry high arousal, anger, danger, and urgency but can also evoke attraction and desire; Yellow Memes mediate warning, attention, light, visibility, and culturally variable meanings; Green Memes express repair and regeneration; Gray Memes blur responsibility through ambiguity and silence; Blue Memes carry calmness, distance, melancholy, institutionality, and sometimes sexual or obscene meanings; and Pink Memes mediate sexual shame, comic embarrassment, and erotic playfulness. Red and Pink are conceptually distinct even when both concern sexuality. The analysis also considers bodily flushing, reproductive coloration, and the context-dependent visibility of redness. The paper introduces meme color weakness, the misrecognition of a meme’s color, and meme blindness, the failure to recognize one’s own actions and expressions as memes. It further develops color translation by comparing examples of sexual coding associated with pink in Japanese, blue in English, and yellow in Chinese. The analysis distinguishes these linguistic conventions from red associated with sexual attraction and from spatial or institutional color coding, illustrated by red-light districts and Japan’s historical red-line and blue-line districts. The framework is applied to sexual memes on social media and organizational communication. Sexual memes can circulate as humor, shame, desire, or obscenity, and can be recoded as contamination, outrage, or ambiguity. Organizational messages similarly change meaning when green improvement is perceived as red attack, yellow warning is dismissed as gray noise, or black labels undermine voice. The paper concludes with a model of color attribution, perception, misrecognition, selection, and memetic re-coding, explaining how social meanings change as memes cross contexts and shape collective behavior.

articles.title: Impact of YouTube Usage on the Academic Performance of Undergraduates at the University of Ilorin
articles.abstract: This quantitative study examines the impact of YouTube usage on the academic performance of undergraduate students at the University of Ilorin, Nigeria. Grounded in Moreno and Mayer’s Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, the research utilises a cross-sectional survey design with a stratified random sample of 400 registered undergraduates across 15 faculties. Data were collected via structured questionnaires and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson Product-Moment Correlation (PPMC), and simple linear regression in SPSS v27. Results reveal high student engagement, with 57.5% spending 1–6 hours daily on YouTube and 85.8% utilising the platform for academic tutorials and research. Statistical analysis demonstrates a significant positive correlation between time spent on YouTube and academic performance ($r = .597, p < .001$). Furthermore, regression analysis indicates that the type of educational content consumed significantly predicts academic performance ($R^2 = .374, \beta = .612, p < .001$). The study concludes that YouTube serves as an effective, self-directed multimedia learning supplement that manages cognitive load and enhances student comprehension, while highlighting the role of digital literacy and self-regulation in optimising learning outcomes.

articles.title: The Local Group Paradox: Small Groups as Incubators of Both Cultural Pathology and Innovation
articles.abstract: This study develops a theoretical explanation for why small local groups can generate two apparently opposing outcomes: cultural pathology and innovation. Rather than treating organizational culture as a uniform property of an entire organization, the study focuses on the smaller interaction environments in which members repeatedly observe, evaluate, imitate, and regulate one another. It distinguishes total organizational size (Norg), local interaction size (Nlocal), the effective norm-forming core (Ncore), and effective cultural population size (Ne, culture), defined as the diversity of behavioral options that actually function within a group. The study combines longitudinal insider observation of an anonymized workplace unit with a publicly documented organizational case based on an independent investigation report and regulatory materials. In the internal case, a local interaction environment of approximately four to five members showed increasing convergence around particular behavioral patterns, whereas the same individual displayed markedly different interpersonal behavior after moving to an environment of approximately 36–38 members. The public case further illustrates that an organization of roughly 180 members may still become culturally localized when decision-making, personnel authority, information, and evaluation are concentrated in a narrow core. Building on cultural evolution, social learning, organizational culture, and network research, this study defines local fixation as a process through which a cultural variant is repeatedly enacted within a local group, becomes disproportionately available relative to alternatives, and eventually functions as a local default. Local fixation may reduce cultural variation within groups while increasing cultural differentiation between groups. Crucially, the same mechanism can generate divergent outcomes. When anger, domination, silence, or exclusion is locally fixed, cultural pathology may emerge; when novel ideas, minority dissent, or unconventional problem-solving practices are locally fixed, the same process may support innovation. This dual outcome is conceptualized as the Local Group Paradox. Small groups do not necessarily preserve cultural diversity; rather, they can amplify particular cultural variants and create local cultural bias. Accordingly, small groups may function both as incubators of pathology and as incubators of innovation. The study further proposes a Nested Locality perspective in which large organizations are understood as cultural ecosystems composed of multiple embedded local groups. The practical implication is not to eliminate locality, but to preserve local autonomy while preventing cultural isolation.

articles.title: Who Speaks in the Candidate's Comment Section? Participation, Toxicity and Reward on Donald Trump's and Hillary Clinton's Facebook Pages in 2016
articles.abstract: In 2016 the comment sections under Donald Trump's and Hillary Clinton's Facebook posts drew millions of comments. Who took part, how hostile were they, and was hostility rewarded? I study 5.2 million comments: every comment that could be retrieved from 730 posts on Trump's page during the Republican primaries (January to April 2016), and from 16 posts on the two candidates' pages on 1 October 2016. Commenters appear only as anonymised codes. A weighted sample of 111,925 comments was scored with an open toxicity classifier and checked against a dictionary measure applied to every comment. Participation was very unequal: the most active 1% of 1.1 million commenters wrote 31% of the comments. About one comment in ten was toxic, and the rate barely moved across the primaries, falling slightly on voting days. Toxicity was not rewarded: once the timing of comments is taken into account, toxic comments were as likely as others on the same post to receive at least one like. The heaviest commenters were no more toxic than occasional ones. On 1 October the two candidates' comment sections were equally toxic, but the 1,106 people who commented on both pages were more toxic on Clinton's page than on Trump's. Hostility in these spaces was widespread rather than concentrated among the most active. Provenance and AI use. The data were collected with Netvizz for my doctoral research, before Netvizz closed in 2019. This paper builds on my doctoral thesis (Hotham 2021, University of Bath). The analysis and writing were completed in 2026. I designed the study and am responsible for the analysis and conclusions. I wrote the text, with drafting and editing assistance from Claude (Anthropic), which also helped prepare the analysis code. I reviewed and checked all text and results.

articles.title: The Emotion Economy: Algorithmic amplification, cognitive fluency, and cultural schemas in Instapoetry
articles.abstract: The contemporary literary landscape has been fundamentally reshaped by the rise of Instapoetry: short, visual, and emotionally direct verse disseminated primarily through Instagram, a platform whose image-first architecture and recommender systems privilege affectively engaging content. This article argues that the dominance of this poetic form represents not a superficial cultural trend but an adaptive response to a digitally mediated attention economy. It advances an integrative theoretical framework explaining Instapoetry through the convergence of three dimensions: algorithmic, psychological, and cultural. First, algorithmic amplification on Instagram leverages patterns of repetition and social proof to promote specific formal styles. Second, the cognitive state of the platform’s users—marked by social media fatigue and elevated cognitive load—produces a preference for content high in processing fluency. Third, the cultural motifs that dominate Instapoetry function as accessible affective schemas, enabling readers to engage in self-expression, identity construction, and emotional validation. Drawing on research in media studies, cognitive science, and feminist literary criticism—and referencing the influential work of early Instapoets such as Rupi Kaur and Amanda Lovelace—this paper proposes a multidisciplinary account of how digital infrastructures and human psychology jointly shape contemporary poetic production and reception.

articles.title: Generative AI and High School Students: Views, Perceptions, and Uses
articles.abstract: This study investigates high school students' awareness, usage patterns, productivity perceptions, aesthetic preferences, and visual discrimination abilities regarding GenAI. Utilizing an online questionnaire surveyed to N= 38 male high school students in Qatar across STEM (60.52%), Business/Commerce (26.31%) and Arts/Humanities (13.15%) streams, the research evaluated both self-reported behavioral data and empirical visual perception performance. Findings reveal that 86.8% of respondents report awareness of GenAI and 57.9% using AI tools on a weekly or daily basis, primarily for studying/research. Rather than passive adoption, 92.1% prefer actively editing AI-generated text prior to final submission, treating GenAI as a drafting assistant. While 100% of respondents acknowledged that GenAI accelerated their output speed, views on output quality were split, with only 44.7% reporting simultaneous speed and quality improvements. In blinded aesthetic preference tasks, participants overwhelming favored AI-generated artwork across 4 image pairs. However, in origin-discrimination tasks, participants achieved an overall detection of 73.02%; however, their accuracy dropped significantly to 60.5% on complex painterly styles. This analysis proves a critical divergence: high operational familiarity and strong aesthetic bias toward synthetic media do not automatically equate to high critical visual literacy. The paper highlights a need for educational systems to integrate algorithmic and visual literacy training to prepare students to critically evaluate and use GenAI to the best of their abilities.
